title: Lightweight async request instrumentation shim for high-throughput runtimes
creator: Ava Mitchell
description: Add a minimal, high-performance request instrumentation shim for async runtimes (async/await event loops and fiber-based runtimes) that provides deterministic trace propagation, lightweight sampling hints, and a compact header normalization layer. The goal is to instrument our SDKs and server frameworks with <1% p50 latency overhead at production throughput while preserving context fidelity for KV cache lookups and prefix caching used by the inference runtime.
acceptance_criteria: Instrumentation shim implemented for Node.js (async_hooks), Python (contextvars), and Rust/Tokio (TaskLocal) with a consistent public SDK surface
End-to-end trace propagation verified across HTTP/gRPC/WS transports with header normalization and loss-tolerant fallbacks
Benchmarked overhead <1% at p50 and <3% at p95 on representative request mixes (small text gen, long-inference calls)
Sampling hint propagation works: sampling decision stable across async boundaries and honored by collector with <100ms decision window
Compatibility tests added for our existing runtime features: KV cache key preservation, prefix caching hints, and retry/fallback flows
Documentation and migration guide published in docs.redwood.ai with code samples for framework integration
Canary rollout plan documented with metric dashboards and rollback criteria
comments: 2026-02-16 - Diego Chen: Initial spike completed. Built prototype using Python contextvars + lightweight carrier wrapper. Verified context survives task switching in uvloop on local benchmark. Next: formalize carrier format and header normalization rules.
2026-02-20 - Priya Kapoor (PM): Align on scope. Focus on three runtimes first (Node/Python/Rust) and provide shim with identical header names. Defer language-specific helpers to follow-up tickets.

2026-02-25 - Diego Chen: Microbenchmarks attached to PR show ~0.6% overhead at 1k rps synthetic; overhead increases to ~2.8% at p95 under heavy GC. Need to add a sampling fast-path and avoid allocations on hot path.

2026-03-03 - Diego Chen: Implemented fast-path that inlines carrier parsing when request header present and falls back to async reconstruction for warm starts. Added unit tests for concurrent context switches.
